full_judgment: 2. The short facts for disposal of the Rule in Civil Revision No. 264 of 2000 are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 243 of 1997 for Specific Performance of Contract in respect of schedule property against the defendants-opposite parties 1-10, stating, in short, that the land under District Dhaka PS Demra Mouja Tara Bari, CS Khatian No. 306 CS Plot No. 647 1.04 acres land in which 0.02 acres was owned and possessed by late Mosleuddin by inheritance, the predecessor of opposite party Nos. 1-9 who executed a Bainapatra on 3-11-82 with the plaintiff-petitioner for sale of 0134 ajusangsha on consideration of value at Taka 13,000 out of which he paid Taka 3000 and the seller handed over vacant possession and thereafter, plaintiff filled up null land by earth and built a chapra house thereon by investing huge sum of money and leased the house on rent to one Md Hafiz on oral agreement and thereafter executed written agreement on 1-3-93 and that the predecessor of defendants as well as they refused to execute sale deed and lodged a complaint by wife of late Moslehuddin before Commissioner who on hearing both the parties directed defendants predecessor to execute sale deed in favour of plaintiff on 18-1-83 and thereafter predecessors of defendant died leaving successors defendant Nos. 1-9 who also avoided to execute sale deed and defendant No. 1 again lodged complaint against husband of plaintiff before the present Ward Commissioner who notified both the parties and upon hearing on 1-5-97 delivered judgment directing the defendants 1-9 to execute sale deed by taking rest dues of Taka 10,000 which was not complied with and defendants issued a legal notice under section 106 of TP Act for eviction and plaintiff replied to the same and filed the suit for Specific Performance of Contract.
